Dear David,

Thank you for taking the time to prepare the proposal. It is evident that a 
great deal of thought and effort went into it. I genuinely appreciate that.

I think you've captured our vision very well.

Rather than marking up the document, I thought it would be easier to send my 
comments in writing. Most of the suggestions below are intended to ensure 
clarity, alignment and flexibility.

1. Section 3 – 8-Month Roadmap

Since our objective is to build a long-term platform rather than complete a 
project within a predetermined 8-month period, I think it would be better to 
present the roadmap as the expected sequence of activities rather than 
assigning them to specific calendar months. Therefore, I would suggest 
replacing the month-by-month structure with project “phases” instead of 
months.

In addition, I would appreciate if we could insert the following sentence 
immediately before the roadmap: "The following roadmap is illustrative only. 
Activities may overlap, be accelerated, or be reordered depending on 
commercial opportunities, brand responsiveness, and the parties’ 
priorities." I think this better reflects the way we will actually work 
together.

2. Section 3 – Korea Visit

On a related matter, I would prefer to remove the reference to the Korea 
visit taking place in Month 6 and instead providing that it may be scheduled 
whenever deemed commercially appropriate by the parties.

Please consider replacing the relevant language with:

“A Korea visit may be scheduled at any point during the engagement whenever 
commercially appropriate and mutually agreed by the parties. The parties 
currently intend to arrange an initial Korea visit during the early stage of 
the engagement, subject to identifying and coordinating meetings with 
suitable priority brands.”

Generally, my preference is to conduct the initial Korea visit relatively 
early in the process. Our ultimate objective is to establish direct, 
long-term relationships with selected brands and, where commercially 
possible, obtain exclusive distribution rights in Israel. A request for 
exclusivity is a significant commitment for a brand, and I believe it will 
be much more credible and effective if we meet the relevant decision-makers 
in person, present Blue Marble’s platform and growth plans directly, and 
begin building trust from the outset.

subject: RE: Exploring a K-Beauty Retail Concept in Israel
body:
Dear David and Gilad,

Thank you again for taking the time to speak with me over the past couple of 
weeks. I appreciate the insights you shared and the opportunity to better 
understand both the Korean beauty industry and the process of building a 
successful multi-brand K-beauty platform.

We would like to move forward.

As you know, our vision is to develop a flagship multi-brand K-beauty 
destination on Dizengoff Square in Tel Aviv, complemented by a robust online 
platform. Assuming the flagship performs as we expect, we anticipate 
expanding to additional locations. We are approaching this as the creation 
of a long-term retail platform rather than a single-store concept.

Blue Marble intends to act as the importer of record and build direct 
relationships with the brands. Our objective is to curate a best-in-class 
assortment while securing exclusive partnerships with selected brands where 
it makes strategic sense. For other brands, we are open to different 
commercial structures depending on what creates the strongest long-term 
platform.

As a next step, I would appreciate receiving a proposal outlining how you 
envision working together. Ideally, I see your team assisting us with:

*	Developing the overall brand and assortment strategy for the platform.
*	Advising on which brands may be appropriate candidates for exclusive 
partnerships and which may be better suited to other commercial 
arrangements.
*	Facilitating introductions and discussions with Korean brand.
*	Providing ongoing strategic guidance as we prepare for launch and begin 
building long-term relationships with the brands.

It would also be helpful if your proposal outlined the recommended roadmap 
for the engagement, and how you see your role evolving as the platform 
hopefully grows.

I would also appreciate your thoughts on the most effective sequence of next 
steps. My initial thought is that, once we align on the engagement, we 
should refine the target brand portfolio together and begin discussions with 
selected Korean brands. If you believe an early trip to Korea would 
accelerate that process, I would be very happy to plan a visit and meet with 
the brands alongside David.

Thank you.

Best regards,

Arielle Cohen

Hi David,

Thank you for your thoughtful response.

To answer your questions:

1.	Timeline – We are targeting the launch of the online platform first, 
with a goal of going live within approximately 6 months. The flagship retail 
store in Tel Aviv would ideally follow shortly thereafter, depending on site 
selection and development timelines.

2.	Distribution Structure – Our preference is to work directly with brands 
whenever possible, particularly for brands where an exclusive partnership 
for Israel may be achievable. However, we remain open to alternative 
structures where they make strategic and commercial sense.

3.	Budget – We are prepared to make a meaningful investment in the concept, 
including inventory, store development, marketing, and operational setup. 
While we are still refining the business plan, the project is being 
approached with a long-term view and sufficient capital to build a leading 
K-beauty platform in Israel rather than a small-scale retail operation.

I agree with your assessment that support will likely be needed across brand 
selection, assortment strategy, introductions, commercial negotiations, and 
the initial onboarding process with brands. This is precisely why I would 
value your involvement.

I would be pleased to review a proposal outlining how you typically support 
new market entries, including the scope of services you would recommend and 
how you envision the process unfolding. If you believe a visit to Korea 
would be beneficial at the appropriate stage, I would certainly be open to 
that as well.

I look forward to hearing your thoughts.

Best regards,

Arielle Cohen

CEO

Blue Marble

I hope you are doing well. 

 

Thank you again for taking the time to speak with me last month. I found
our discussion extremely valuable and it reinforced my belief that there
is an opportunity to build a differentiated K-beauty platform in Israel if
approached thoughtfully. After spending additional time reviewing both the
market and the brands in your portfolio, I have decided that I would like
to move forward with exploring this concept more intensely.

 

Our vision remains centered around creating a curated, experiential
flagship destination in Tel Aviv, supported by a strong online platform.
Rather than simply building another cosmetics store, we are focused on
creating a trusted platform for Korean beauty in Israel.

 

Several of the brands you represent stood out to me as particularly
interesting, including Mixsoon, Arencia, Sungboon Editor, Nooni, Grabity,

different structures for others.

assortment, evaluating brand opportunities, and establishing relationships
with the companies that could become part of the concept.

 

At this point, I would be interested in hearing your thoughts on the most
logical next step. 

 

I am certainly open to traveling to Korea if you believe that would be the

subject: SV: Re: Re: Re: [Yogico] Introducing Osstem Pharma & Vussen Business Overview
body:
Hello David,

I hope that you are doing well.

Thank you for the explanation below and for clarifying the distinction 
between the B2B activities managed by Osstem Implant and the B2C activities 
managed by Osstem Pharma.

We are pleased to hear that Vussen is open to discussing exclusivity for the 
Turkish B2C market, provided that the commercial terms can be aligned.

As mentioned in my previous email, we have finalized discussions with our 
retailers and our first retail partner, Rossmann Turkey, is ready to launch 
Vussen in 204 stores. Rossmann is one of the leading health, beauty, and 
personal care retail chains in Turkey, making it an excellent starting point 
for the brand.

Following the launch in Rossmann, we plan to expand distribution to Watsons 
Turkey, the country’s largest beauty and personal care retailer with more 
than 400 stores nationwide, as well as MakroCenter, a premium supermarket 
chain targeting higher-income consumers and imported brands. We believe this 
phased rollout strategy will create a strong foundation for sustainable 
growth and long-term brand development.

Based on our current retail discussions and planned distribution strategy, 
our estimated sales forecast is as follows:

*	Year 1: 120,000 units
*	Year 2: 250,000 units
*	Year 3: 300,000–500,000 units

These figures are based on a conservative and achievable approach. As 
distribution expands and brand awareness grows through our marketing 
investments and retailer partnerships, we believe there is significant 
upside potential beyond these estimates.

Our company has successfully built more than 30 brands in Turkey, taking 
them from launch to becoming top-performing brands within their respective 
categories. We therefore have extensive experience in brand building, retail 
execution, and developing long-term partnerships with key retailers.

Considering the retailer commitment already secured and the investments 
required to launch and develop the brand successfully, we believe 
exclusivity is essential for us to move forward and make the necessary 
long-term commitments to Vussen in the Turkish market.

We look forward to receiving further information regarding the exclusivity 
agreement and to building a successful long-term partnership together.

Best Regards,

Okan Can
